evidence.quote: We pair the benchmark with the existing official JSON Schema Test Suite and evaluate six state-of-the-art constrained decoding frameworks
a collection of 10K real-world JSON schemas from various sources, Organized into 10 datasets of varying complexity and diversity
We start with the 6K JSON schemas collected by Baazizi et al. [2021] from publicly available GitHub repositories
with GitHub-Ultra serving as an aspirational target for future advancements
We used Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with the Llamacpp inference engine as backend for Outlines, Guidance, and Llamacpp.
While Outlines and Llamacpp demonstrate substantially lower throughput than the LM-only approach, Guidance achieves even higher efficiency
Outlines, which converts JSON schemas into regular-expression based constraints, has significantly higher compilation time.
we add an additional experiment with the Hugging Face Transformers inference engine for XGrammar and Guidance. All values are median of the result samples.
We use greedy decoding with zero-temperature, performing a single generation run, and enforce a 40-second timeout for grammar compilation and an additional 40 seconds for generation.
Guidance shows the highest empirical coverage on six out of the eight datasets, with Llamacpp taking the lead on the remaining two

LM-only exhibits the lowest compliance rate, highlighting its unreliability as a standalone solution. While closed-source implementations have low empirical coverage, they have very high compliance rates
Empirical coverage between Open Source engines and OpenAI/Gemini are not directly comparable due to differences in the underlying model
The test suite organizes its test cases into 45 categories, each of which corresponds to a feature of JSON Schema
Guidance outperforms other engines at all coverage levels, achieving full coverage on 13 categories and moderate coverage on 21.
Llamacpp and XGrammar have full coverage on only one category and moderate coverage on five and three categories, respectively, while Outlines has no full coverage on any category
In contrast, XGrammar minimizes compilation errors but shows the highest number of under-constrained failures, indicating a trade-off favoring permissiveness.
For our experiments, we use the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model to measure task performance.
The outputs for all three tasks are structured as JSON objects with two fields: "reasoning" and "answer"
The results in Table 8 show that the constrained decoding, regardless of the framework, achieves higher performance than the unconstrained setting.
We believe this may be attributed to its token-healing implementation
